subject: Post-call: Evaluation framework & hosting recommendation for DataWorks trial
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@dataworks.com>, Alex Morales <alex.morales@dataworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Evaluation framework & hosting recommendation for DataWorks trial

Hi Laura / Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have a single source of truth for the trial planning. I captured the items we agreed on and added a recommended hosting approach based on your tech constraints. Please reply with any corrections or approvals.

Summary of needs (from your team)
- Primary goal: Validate realtime classification quality on in-house documents and integrated search latency under 300ms p95 for 1–2k QPS.
- Data sensitivity: Customer PII + regulatory requirement for audit logs; prefers tenant isolation.
- Network: Private VPC-to-VPC peering with strict egress controls is desired but not mandatory for MVP.
- Timeline: 4-week evaluation window starting mid-Jan; decision meeting scheduled at end of month 4.

Success criteria (proposal)
1) Quality: F1 >= 0.82 on your labeled holdout set and zero major functional regressions vs your baseline.
2) Latency: p95 <= 300ms for typical prompt size (avg 120 tokens).
3) Cost proxy: Per-request cost within 2x of internal budget estimate (we will provide rough numbers).
4) Operational: Audit logs retained for 90 days and token-level usage visibility in console.

Hosting options (pros/cons — high level)
- Hosted (Redwood API): Fastest to spin up, lowest friction for integration, but shared tenancy; acceptable if DataWorks keeps no raw PII in requests.
- Dedicated Sandbox (recommended): Isolated GPU pool, predictable throughput, supports canary & scaling policies. Good balance of isolation and time-to-value.
- VPC Private Deployment: Full VPC peering + customer-managed networking and KMS — meets highest security bar but adds 2–3 weeks of networking setup and an on-prem checklist.

Our recommendation: start with a Dedicated Sandbox for the 4-week trial (meets isolation + throughput needs) with a short pilot on Hosted for integration testing if you want to start earlier. If DataWorks needs strict egress or HSM-backed keys, plan for a VPC trial in parallel as follow-up.

Proposed evaluation plan & ownership
- Week 0 (pre-setup): Network checklist + credentials exchange (DataWorks owner: Laura; Redwood owner: Karthik).
- Week 1: Integration smoke tests (Hosted staging) + dataset ingest. (SE owner: Marissa)
- Week 2–3: Dedicated sandbox run for load & quality tests; daily monitoring. (Ops/SE: Marissa + Redwood infra)
- Week 4: Final analysis, quality regression check, cost estimate, and decision meeting. (All)

Deliverables we will share this week:
- Environment comparison spreadsheet (attached)
- Network requirements checklist (attachment)
- Mutual action plan doc (attachment)

Ask from you
1) Confirm the three success criteria above or propose revisions.
2) Share any internal compliance gates we should plan for (legal/infosec contact).
3) Confirm availability for a 30-min prep call next Thu (Dec 10) to lock down Week 0 tasks.

If that all looks good, we will provision a Dedicated Sandbox template and send the initial access tokens + a one-click integration guide.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood-environment-options.xlsx (spreadsheet), DW-network-requirements.pdf (PDF), mutual-action-plan.docx (docx)
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@dataworks.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Evaluation framework & hosting recommendation for DataWorks trial

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Quality metric: we can commit to the F1 holdout target, but we need to run at least three datasets (support tickets, product docs, and internal wiki) to feel confident. Is that OK for the sandbox?
- Latency: 300ms p95 is aggressive for our current infra; can we also capture p50/p99 in the dashboard?
- Data flow: For the first two weeks, we prefer to keep data transfer via S3 ingest (no live peering). If sandbox setup requires peering, we can do S3-based ingestion as a fallback.

Also, a couple of asks for procurement/legal:
- Can you confirm Redwood's standard data retention & deletion process for trial data?
- We will need a one-page outline of the security controls (SOC2 scope, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS options) for our security team to review.

We are OK starting the timeline mid-Jan but want to ensure Week 0 tasks are completed beforehand. I can be on the prep call Dec 10.

Cheers,
Laura
Laura Chen | Head of ML Platforms
DataWorks Corp
laura.chen@dataworks.com

Hi all —

Thanks Ben. Quick technical answers and next steps from my side:

1) Datasets & ingest
- Dedicated Sandbox: supports mounting multiple S3 prefixes as separate corpora; we can tag runs by dataset. No VPC peering required for S3-based ingestion. Good for Week 1 onboarding + Week 2–3 runs.
- Hosted staging: easiest for early integration tests (we'll provide a temp API key and IP allowlist).

2) Performance guidance
- For LlamaX-13B quantized with our kernel path and continuous batching, we expect p95 ~ 180–280ms at 1k QPS for avg 120-token prompts on a 4-GPU dedicated pool. p99 will be higher — expect spikes ~450ms under bursty loads. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 in the console.

3) Security & compliance note (summary)
- SOC2: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II for hosted and Dedicated control planes; audit report can be shared under NDA.
- Encryption: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest. Dedicated Sandbox keys can be customer-managed via KMS integration if you require.
- Audit logs: we retain user and token-level logs for 90 days by default for trials; longer retention available as an add-on.

4) Timeline & immediate asks
- I will attach: network checklist and a one-page security summary (see attachments).
- Karthik, if you can provide cost deltas, I will draft the Week 0 checklist and a pre-provision form for Dedicated Sandbox so we can provision immediately after the prep call.

Laura — happy to confirm Dec 10 for a 30-min prep call at 09:00 PT. Ben, do you want me to run the integration checklist on the call?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
